clue.text: Anti-profiteering agreement?

parts.note: split the word in two and it reads as an instruction to prohibit profit, a bar on making a gain; read whole it is a deal struck between buyer and seller

explanation.surface: A pact between firms to stop anyone cashing in unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BAR GAIN, the word itself is 'anti-profiteering': to bar is to forbid, and gain is profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal or pact struck between two parties is a synonym, as in 'drive a hard one'.

clue.text: Stupid railwayman prohibited said players?

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway
an ass is a stupid person

indicators.note: said signals that the word for prohibited is heard rather than written

parts.note: banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: A dim railway worker banned, so he says, from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' turns BANNED into BAND by sound; BR, for British Rail, stands for the railwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of musicians on trumpets, cornets and tubas are players, a fair description.

clue.text: Girl goes to one S. American port or another

parts.note: Rosa is a girl's name
another South American port, Rio de Janeiro

explanation.surface: A girl travels to one South American harbour or a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second port, Rio, joined to ROSA; Rosario is a river port in Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine city on the Paraná is a major inland port of South America.

clue.text: Loss of civil rights for Dr Tate in a riot

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters before it are thrown into a jumble

explanation.surface: A doctor named Tate is stripped of his rights after taking part in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riot' scrambles DR TATE IN A; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The old legal penalty of forfeiting property and civic status on conviction for treason or felony.

clue.text: Inspiring figure?

parts.note: the figure is a number, and the inspiring ones are the Muses, how many of them there were

explanation.surface: Someone who motivates others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' means a number, not a person: there were that many Muses inspiring the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The count of the Muses of Greek myth, the goddesses who inspired artists.

clue.text: Possibly tides full of river silt?

indicators.note: full of says the shuffled letters hold the river's letters inside them
possibly signals that the letters of the word tides may be rearranged into another order

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A musing on whether the tides carry a river's silt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the anagram and 'full of' the container; 'tides' looks like the subject of the sentence but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt is sediment laid down by water, which is the geological sense of a layer left behind.

clue.text: No satisfaction with record concerning wine

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
on means about or concerning
tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Being unhappy with a recording about wine.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a red wine from Spain, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissatisfaction or unrest is a synonym for a lack of contentment.

clue.text: Upsetting to a big cheese on whom all turns

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means turned upside down, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: Unsettling for an important boss on whom everything depends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' turns TO VIP upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A central person or point around which everything rotates or depends.

clue.text: Able to pay in new £5 notes

indicators.note: in places the money inside the rearranged notes
new signals the word notes appears in a fresh form, its letters rearranged

parts.note: L is the pound sign and V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Able to settle up with crisp new five-pound notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges NOTES to SOENT, and 'in' puts L (pound) and V (five) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having enough money to meet debts, a synonym for financially sound.

clue.text: People securing certain ranks?

definitions.meaning: those who tie or fasten things
rows or levels, as in a stadium or a hierarchy

explanation.surface: Those who hold certain positions.
explanation.walkthrough: One reading is a coined word, those who tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows set one above another are levels, and those who fasten knots are tie-makers.

clue.text: Advantage point in a number of games

indicators.note: in says the point is placed inside the letters for a number of games

parts.note: a set in tennis is a group of games
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tennis player gaining the upper hand at a key point in a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point, S, not a point scored; it goes inside A SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit or strength is a synonym, as in a quality that is valuable to a team.

clue.text: Dandy town in USA?

parts.note: Beau Nash was the famous eighteenth-century dandy of Bath
ville is French for town, and a common ending of American place names

explanation.surface: A question about a fashionable place in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard 'Beau' Nash was the leader of fashion in Georgian Bath; the whole clue describes the Tennessee city as a dandy's town.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tennessee, famed for country music, is a city in the United States.

clue.text: Noted race?

definitions.meaning: set to musical notes, so a melody or tune
a race in the sense of a breed, stock or line of descent

explanation.surface: A celebrated contest, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' looks like 'famous', but here it means made of notes, a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is both a passage of music and a breed or stock of animals or plants.

clue.text: Vain — but deficient in nether wear

definitions.meaning: in vain, useless, to no avail

explanation.surface: Someone's vanity undercut by their having nothing on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' means futile here, not conceited; the old word for futile is also, read literally, 'without boots'.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile effort is an old synonym, and lacking footwear is the literal reading of the word.

clue.text: Manage to apply some remedy, perhaps

definitions.meaning: run or govern, as an estate

explanation.surface: Contriving to give someone a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an organisation and to dispense medicine are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Shun a vacuum

parts.note: a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: Keep away from a vacuum cleaner, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun something is to steer clear of it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Took away document about land

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the document is placed around the land

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Someone removed the paperwork concerning a piece of property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but here it means going around, so the document wraps the land.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away from a reputation or merit is to diminish it, a synonym.

clue.text: Play with songs?

parts.note: play is a verb, to provide music along with a singer, not a staged drama featuring songs

explanation.surface: A drama with musical numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a noun (a musical); it is the verb of an accompanist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist backing a singer does this, playing alongside the vocal line.

clue.text: Censure side rioting round parts of Paris

indicators.note: round says the shuffled side letters go around the other pieces
rioting suggests disorder, so the letters of side run wild into a new order
parts of suggests the word Paris broken up and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Condemning one faction rampaging through districts of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'rioting' scrambles SIDE into DISE and 'parts of' scrambles PARIS into PRAIS, which 'round' places within DISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Blame or disapproval, an old synonym, the opposite of commendation.

clue.text: Abandoning replacement one's tried

indicators.note: replacement signals the letters are put back in a different place, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Giving up on a substitute after testing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacement' rearranges the letters of ONES TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving behind a post or spouse is the act of quitting, so the gerund matches the noun.

clue.text: Goes on foot when best man goes on a bike

parts.note: ST, saint, is a man of the best kind
rides means travels on a bicycle

explanation.surface: The best man walks while the wedding party cycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' is not the wedding role but a saint, ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with long steps is a synonym for walking on foot.

clue.text: Dr Watson's patients recorded in Holmes's book?

definitions.text: Dr Watson's patients recorded in Holmes's book?

parts.words: Dr Watson's patients recorded in Holmes's book?
parts.note: a doctor's patients are his clinical matters, while what Sherlock Holmes's chronicler records are the detective's investigations; one word covers both

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Watson wrote up his medical patients in a Holmes story.
explanation.walkthrough: Watson was both a doctor and the narrator of the Sherlock Holmes stories, so the word fits medical and detective work alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's patients and a detective's investigations are both referred to as instances to handle.

clue.text: Main ATS formation showed .staying-power

indicators.note: formation signals the letters are drawn up into a new arrangement, like troops

explanation.surface: The main ATS unit showed endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance or resilience is a synonym.

clue.text: Scornful of many in love with doctor, since retired

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the whole string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a crowd of people in love with a doctor who has stopped practising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns the whole run C-IN-O-DR-AS backwards; 'of' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and cynical, so a synonym for contemptuous.

clue.text: Judge's condition is serious, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the state of a judge in the saying about being as clear-headed as one

explanation.surface: A judge's state is grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'as ___ as a judge' means completely clear-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Not drunk, as in the idiom about a judge, and also grave or solemn in manner.

clue.text: See through this college?

definitions.meaning: a window you look through, a projecting bay

explanation.surface: Is this college transparent?
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the projecting upper-storey window; the other is the Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay window projecting from an upper floor, and also an Oxford college.

clue.text: Injure one with a prim disposition

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: disposition, an arrangement or placing, signals that a and prim are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Harming someone who has a prudish nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' looks like temperament, but it means arrangement: A PRIM becomes MPAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or weaken something is a synonym, as of hearing or health.

clue.text: Bird lost head in island

indicators.note: lost head says the first letter of the bird's name is dropped

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird beheaded on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: An inch is a small island, a word found in Scottish place names such as Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and Irish word for a small islet.

clue.text: Poor potter gets game

parts.note: poor means bad, of low quality
Thomas Minton founded the Staffordshire pottery firm of that name

explanation.surface: An inept potter gets a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' is a proper noun here: Minton is the English china maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net is an example of a game.

clue.text: A little party, one of ten minutes on stage

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A brief political get-together, one lasting ten minutes on the boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten Minute Alibi' was a 1933 stage thriller by Anthony Armstrong; the definition points to the last word of its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The play Ten Minute Alibi gives the word a stage version lasting ten minutes.

clue.text: Thief of the lower type?

parts.note: lower is read as one that lows, a cow, so the thief steals cattle rather than being of a base sort

explanation.surface: A small-time crook of the humbler kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' rhymes with 'mower' here: cattle low, so a lower is a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief of the American West is called this.

clue.text: A boat by the water here in Merseyside

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Someone moors a boat beside the water in Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoylake is a seaside town on the Wirral, in Merseyside, near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wirral resort town lies in the Merseyside county, so it is a place there.
